chapter: Records, dances and Blanche Calloway (repeated passages)
title: Few new records and listening to them on the road
summary: Ten new records a month was a lot then; he could not afford a phonograph on the road and listened when at home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Mmm-hmm. Musicians listened to those records a lot, I guess.

Yeah. Well, you didn't get very many records during the year. Like, the market is flooded with records now. But in them days, if ten records came out in a month...if ten new records came out a month, it was doing great, you know. Now they've got so many records coming out every month, you can't keep up with them.
A lot of things get lost that way, too.
But I guess if a new Louis Hot Five or Hot Seven came out, something like that, everybody would listen to it.
Because those solos... You know some of them by heart.
Yeah. I used to listen... I used to keep my ears open, you know.
Did you carry a phonograph with you on the road?
Oh, no. I couldn't afford a phonograph.
So when did you listen to records?
Whenever I got a chance to.
Like if you went to somebody's house or something?
Yes. When I was at home I used to get records, buy records every now and then -- get a record.
